claim: PUMS's Fall 2027 application calendar gives the start of classes as 13 September 2026 — a 2026 day printed on a 2027 calendar — and puts orientation week at 6–12 September 2027.
excerpt: Start of classes: 13 Sep 2026 […] Orientation week for incoming students in Poznan: 6 - 12 Sep 2027
interpretation: The date is internally impossible: a 2027 intake cannot begin classes in September 2026. What makes this page the more informative of the two is its orientation week, 6–12 September 2027, because PUMS runs classes after orientation rather than during it — for 2026/27 it published orientation 7–13 September and classes 14 September. That pattern points at Monday 13 September 2027, which would make the '13 Sep' here the right day with the wrong year. It is still an inference, the string appears on no PUMS page, and the product records no date.

notes: Neither PUMS page carries a last-updated stamp, so there is no way to tell which of the two figures is the stale one.

claim: PUMS's medicine admission-requirements page, under a heading for Fall 2027 entry, gives the start of classes as 6 September 2027.
interpretation: This has the right year, which makes it the tempting one, and it collides with the university's own orientation week of 6–12 September 2027 on the calendar page recorded as ev-pums-calendar-class-start. Classes cannot start on the Monday orientation begins. So the page with the correct year is not thereby the correct page, and neither figure can be published as printed. This is the specific reason the entry carries no date rather than the later or the more plausible one: a medical degree is a six-year commitment and a student moving to Poznan a week early or a week late is a real cost.

notes: The resolution is not ours to make; it needs the PUMS admissions office. The country record says so and records what the evidence points at without publishing it.

publisher: Sejm of the Republic of Poland - Law on Higher Education and Science (Dz.U. 2018 poz. 1668, consolidated text)
claim: A Polish public university may charge for study in a foreign language, and the statutory fee exemption for EU/EEA/Swiss citizens covers only full-time study in Polish.
excerpt: Art. 79. 1. Uczelnia publiczna może pobierać opłaty za usługi edukacyjne związane z: […] 3) kształceniem na studiach w języku obcym; […] 5) kształceniem cudzoziemców na studiach stacjonarnych w języku polskim. […] Art. 324. […] 2. Opłat, o których mowa w art. 79 ust. 1 pkt 5, nie pobiera się od: 1) cudzoziemca – obywatela państwa członkowskiego Unii Europejskiej, Konfederacji Szwajcarskiej lub państwa członkowskiego Europejskiego Porozumienia o Wolnym Handlu (EFTA) – strony umowy o Europejskim Obszarze Gospodarczym i członków ich rodzin, mieszkających na terytorium Rzeczypospolitej Polskiej
interpretation: Art. 79(1) pt 3 (foreign-language study) is a fee a public university may charge anyone, Polish citizens included. Art. 324(2) exempts EU/EEA/Swiss citizens from the pt 5 fee only, which is the foreigner fee on full-time Polish-language study. So the statute neither charges nor exempts an EU citizen on an English-taught programme: each university decides in its own fee rules (art. 80(2)). Whether 'mieszkających na terytorium Rzeczypospolitej Polskiej' (living in Poland) binds the citizen or only the family members is not settled by the text; universities paraphrase it both ways.

notes: Consolidated text dated 2026-08-03 in its page footers, built on t.j. Dz.U. 2024 poz. 1571 with amendments to 2026 poz. 912. An amendment to art. 79 takes effect on 1 January 2027 (see the country profile); the text seen does not change points 3 and 5.

attestation.by: the issue #41 research pass (Poland EU route)
attestation.note: isap.sejm.gov.pl serves an Incapsula bot wall to plain HTTP clients; the record page was opened in a browser and its linked 'tekst ujednolicony' PDF (D20181668Lj.pdf) was read from the Sejm's own ELI API, which the ISAP page links as 'API'. publisher: Wroclaw University of Science and Technology - Rector's ordinance ZW 115/2025
claim: Wroclaw Tech charges the foreign-language tuition fee only to 'cudzoziemcy', a term its fee rules define to exclude EU, EEA, Swiss and UK citizens, so full-time English-taught study is free for EU citizens.
excerpt: 8) cudzoziemiec- osoba fizyczna nieposiadająca obywatelstwa polskiego i niebędąca obywatelem państwa członkowskiego Unii Europejskiej, Konfederacji Szwajcarskiej, Zjednoczonego Królestwa Wielkiej Brytanii i Irlandii Północnej, państw członkowskich Europejskiego Stowarzyszenia Wolnego Handlu (EFTA) […] § 2. 1. Uczelnia pobiera opłaty za usługi edukacyjne na studiach związane z: […] 3) kształceniem cudzoziemców na studiach w języku obcym
interpretation: The university's English page says the same in plain words: English-taught programmes are charged to all foreign nationals, with a footnote that this 'does not apply' to EU/EEA/Swiss/UK citizens 'in accordance with ZW115/2025'. Its 2026/27 price list (ZW 72/2026, annex 'od cudzoziemców') is therefore the non-EU price. EU applicants use the 'Free of charge studies' route, which shares the IRK system and timetable with the fee-paying route. The definition, like the statute, ends 'i członków ich rodzin mieszkających na terytorium Rzeczypospolitej Polskiej'; the English footnote attaches the residence condition to family members, and the scholarship page states the EU exemption with no residence condition.

notes: ZW 115/2025 of 25 September 2025 is listed as the fee rules in force for 2026/27 on https://rekrutacja.pwr.edu.pl/dla-cudzoziemcow-akty-prawne/. No 2027/28 acts were published by 30 September 2026.

claim: AGH sets English-taught fees by citizenship: one annex for Polish citizens and another for all students without Polish citizenship, EU citizens included, so an EU citizen pays the same English-taught fee as a non-EU student.
excerpt: § 1. WYSOKOŚĆ OPŁAT POBIERANYCH OD STUDENTÓW POSIADAJĄCYCH OBYWATELSTWO POLSKIE […] § 2. interpretation: Annex 2 (Polish citizens, English-taught) lists a first-cycle fee only for Computer Science, 3,000 EUR a semester. The EU exemption on AGH's international fees page is for full-time study in Polish only.
